collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 4-9 and an adult)

collection.description: A small child has room for only one of three shells: take the choice seriously, or suggest carrying all three.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found three shells on the beach, but (subject.he/she) only has room in (subject.his/her) little bag for one. This is clearly the most important decision of (subject.his/her) life. (subject.He/she) asks (friend) for help, and holds up all three, one after the other, with enormous seriousness.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) squats down and examines each shell with great care. "This one's very shiny," (friend.he/she) says. "This one has a hole, so you could put it on a string. This one has a crab living in it." (subject) gasps and looks inside. There IS a crab. (subject) puts that one back very gently. Then (subject.he/she) takes the one with the hole. "For a necklace," (subject.he/she) explains.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Why not carry two in your hands?" says (friend). (subject) stares at (friend.him/her) as if (friend.he/she) is a genius. (subject.He/she) carries one in the bag and one in each hand, all the way home, not touching anything else. At home (subject.he/she) discovers one of them has a crab living in it. The crab is carried all the way back to the beach. It was a big day.
